To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pain is a frequent sequel of quadrantectomy and radio therapy, (2) pain is mainly described as a cramping and aching, (3) pain generally starts within three months after the completion therapy, (4) pain is mainly localized in the axilla, (5) pain is generally intermittent, (6) pain is related to the patients’ quality of the life.
pain is a frequent sequelae of quadrantectomy and radio-therapy, and that it is associated with worse quality of life in breast cancer patients.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and the management of the pain that may occur after quadrantectomy and postoperative radiotherapy for BC, and that may have an impact on patients’ QOL.
the need to improve the management of pain after CBS and radiotherapy.
the relationship between pain and QL after breast cancer surgery, and suggests that pain may be a significant cause of post-surgery psychosocial distress.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CBS is a valid alternative to mastectomy in early-stage BC, but it is not able to improve QL in all patients, and that pain is a major cause of QL impairment after conservative treatment.
the pain after breast surgery and radiotherapy is frequent, and that it is associated with a negative effect on QL.
pain is a relevant problem for patients who underwent CBS and radiotherapy and that it should be taken into account in clinical practice and research.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pain after breast cancer treatment is common and is associated with worse physical, psychological, and social outcomes.
the pain experienced by patients after CBS and radiotherapy is a relevant factor influencing patients’ QL, and that it should be considered in the postoperative follow-up.
patients who suffer from pain have a significantly poorer QL, especially in the domains of physical well-being, psychological adjustment, physical autonomy, relationships, and social life.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pain is a very common problem after CBS and radiotherapy for early-stage breast cancer, and that it is related to a worse QL.
the assessment of pain after quadrantectomy and adjuvant radiotherapy should be included in the routine evaluation of the patient.
pain after breast surgery and radiotherapy can be severe and long-lasting.
